_readme: THE strobe registry. Every strobe name a task profile may reference is declared
here, and names resolve to numbers against this file and nothing else.
APPEND-ONLY IS A HARD RULE, NOT A CONVENTION. Downstream analysis depends on codes
and their ordering, and historical comparability is a hard requirement. A code is
never repurposed and never renumbered. Adding one means: pick the next free number
from `free_ranges`, give it a `rationale`, and bump nothing -- adding a code does
not bump `vocab_version`, because additions cannot break an existing task.
`vocab_version` bumps only if this file's SHAPE changes.
THE ONE TIME CODES WERE DELETED, and the test that has to be met before it
happens again. On 2026-08-09 thirty-four numbers were reclaimed: the port-slot
families for response ports 3-7, and three codes belonging to a task-graph
interpreter that was removed. Deleting from an append-only registry is normally
the exact mistake this file exists to prevent -- so the bar was not 'nothing uses
them now', it was NO RECORDED SESSION HAS EVER CONTAINED THEM. Every one was
declared for firmware that never ran an animal, and the archive was checked
rather than assumed. A code that has been emitted ONCE, to a file that still
exists, can never be reclaimed on any argument at all -- it goes to `retired`
instead, which is what happened to the dummy-solenoid clicks below.
SOURCE OF TRUTH. Codes with origin 'firmware' mirror BehaviorBox.h and their
numbers are fixed by ~4 years of recorded sessions. Codes with origin 'ephymeris'
were declared by this app: the app's code generator writes them into the firmware
header and into a profile's strobes{} map from this one file, which is what
retires the three-way hand-mirroring the numbers used to live in (BehaviorBox.h,
each sketch's task.json, and a generated C header).
DECLARED MEANS EMITTABLE. Ephymeris docs/tasks.md records a real bug where
GRGL_Sim declared 23 of 31 codes and emitted codes it had not declared; nothing
errored and each layer degraded silently. The inverse is equally a bug, and it is
what the reclamation above corrected: thirty numbers sat here describing ports a
two-port trial runner has no way to poll. Do not add a code on a hunch that
something might want it one day.
The test is whether a code has a MECHANISM that produces it, not whether a task
already does. ODOR_7_ON..ODOR_12_ON are the live example: BoxStrobes.h defines
them, the trial-table editor offers all twelve lines, and a profile that binds
line 7 emits one the moment it runs. Twelve odor lines have always existed in the
pinout and for years only six could announce an onset, which made lines 7-12
plumbed and unusable as discriminanda.
ODOR ONSETS RUN 101-109 AND THEN 114-116, and the jump is the sharpest reason
nothing may compute a code from an index. 110-113 are retired -- the dummy
solenoid clicks, in 29 recorded sessions -- so odor 9 is 109 and odor 10 is 114.
The first six were 101-106 from the beginning and the rest were numbered to
continue that run as closely as the reserved block allows; they briefly sat at
400-405, which no session ever recorded.
PORT SLOTS. `port_slots` below maps a response port's slot number to the six
codes it reports with. There are TWO, because the trial runner has two:
`checkResponse()` in BehaviorBox.h polls `rightWell` and `leftWell` and nothing
else. Slots 1 and 2 are the historical _L and _R families, so the recorded
archive decodes unchanged. A response channel declares its slot in
channels.v1.json, which is what lets everything downstream stop knowing about
left and right -- and a third port declared in the wiring editor is refused by
RIG104 rather than silently reporting nothing, which is the honest answer while
the firmware cannot poll it.

Six codes already exceed 255 (256, 257, 258, 262, 357, 369), so nothing may store
_free_ranges_why: Gaps in the firmware numbering. Non-contiguous and non-patterned, which is why the compiler must look codes up rather than compute them. NOTE the 107-220 gap is split around 110-113: those are retired, not free -- see `retired` below.

START_SESSION.rationale: Anchors every timestamp in the run. Emitted by the sketch loop, not by a trial node.

LIGHTS_ON.emitted_on: entry to the engagement window (trial cue on)
LIGHTS_ON.rationale: The trial-available edge. Paired with nothing; its partner LIGHTS_OFF is not.

LAZY_RAT.rationale: Abstention. No stimulus was presented, so the trial carries no evidence about discrimination and is scored invalid. See BehaviorBox.h:1158-1159.

ODOR_POKE.rationale: Separates an incidental beam-break from a committed initiation. NOTE: does NOT clear the abstention escalator -- BehaviorBox.h:1171-1174 closed that loophole deliberately.

ODOR_UNPOKE_EARLY.rationale: A commitment or sampling hold released early. Emitted from two distinct firmware sites (BehaviorBox.h:1181 pre-odor, :1197 sampling) with the same code, so the two are indistinguishable downstream. See open question in docs/spikes/avr-ram.md.

ODOR_UNPOKE.emitted_on: entry to the response window, after a complete sample
ODOR_UNPOKE.rationale: Withdrawal from the odor port is the sampling/response boundary. The pair order is INVERTED relative to the three abort paths (BehaviorBox.h:1210 then :1213) -- this is why paired strobes are modelled as ordered nodes rather than as a set. See docs/decisions.md D2.

LIGHTS_OFF.emitted_on: entry to a zero-duration node that clears the trial light
LIGHTS_OFF.rationale: Always co-emitted with a behavioural code, never alone, and its ORDER relative to that partner varies by path. Modelled as its own zero-duration node so the order is authored rather than implicit.

INVALID_TRIAL.rationale: The counter does not advance and the same trial binding is re-presented, so an unsampled trial never enters the record as a choice. Emitted by the sketch loop today, not by runTrial().

END_CORRECT_ITI.rationale: Scores correct, advances the counter, clears penalty escalation. Kept distinct from END_INCORRECT_ITI so reinforcement rate and timeout cost are separable.

END_INCORRECT_ITI.rationale: Reached by THREE distinct outcomes -- wrong port, omission, and response-hold failure (BehaviorBox.h:1225) -- so outcome class is NOT recoverable from this code alone. It is recoverable from the preceding strobe, which is exactly why the invariant matters.

END_SESSION.rationale: The clean-stop sentinel. Ephymeris keys its only hardcoded strobe string off this (sessions/runner.py:36).

ODOR_OFF.emitted_on: entry to the sampling-release WAIT_EXIT, and to an inter-stimulus gap
ODOR_OFF.rationale: Odor cleared and vacuum reopened. Reused for the inter-stimulus gap in chained-sampling tasks: the emitter-off event is the same physical event.

WATER_POKE_L.emitted_on: entry to the response branch node, left channel
WATER_POKE_L.rationale: Emitted BEFORE correctness is known (BehaviorBox.h:1082 vs :1093). This is why the response branch is its own zero-duration node with the guard on its edges. See docs/decisions.md D3. Doubles as the false-alarm code on go/no-go.

WATER_POKE_R.emitted_on: entry to the response branch node, right channel

WATER_UNPOKE_EARLY_L.emitted_on: entry to the response-hold-failure penalty, left
WATER_UNPOKE_EARLY_L.rationale: The correct port was reached but released before the hold completed -- a consummatory failure, not a wrong choice. Scored separately so it never contaminates the discrimination measure.

WATER_UNPOKE_EARLY_R.emitted_on: entry to the response-hold-failure penalty, right

FLUID_L.emitted_on: entry to the left reward PULSE
FLUID_L.rationale: Emitted before the solenoid opens (BehaviorBox.h:1047). Pulse width is the delivered volume.

FLUID_R.emitted_on: entry to the right reward PULSE

WATER_UNPOKE_L.emitted_on: entry to the ITI delay, after leaving the left well
WATER_UNPOKE_L.rationale: The only place the firmware observes the end of a consummatory bout, which makes it the anchor for consumption-duration measures. Not emitted on a wrong-well answer -- BehaviorBox.h:1108-1113 returns immediately without awaiting withdrawal.

WATER_UNPOKE_R.emitted_on: entry to the ITI delay, after leaving the right well

WATER_POKE_NONE.emitted_on: entry to the correct terminal path on a withhold trial
WATER_POKE_NONE.rationale: Correct withholding. Already fully implemented in firmware (BehaviorBox.h:1115-1133) although no shipped sketch instantiates isGo=false today, so go/no-go reuses an existing code rather than needing a new one.

WATER_POKE_ERROR_L.emitted_on: entry to the wrong-port penalty, left
WATER_POKE_ERROR_L.rationale: A genuine discrimination error: sampling completed and a choice was expressed, so it advances the session rather than repeating.

WATER_POKE_ERROR_R.emitted_on: entry to the wrong-port penalty, right

STOP_FLUID_G_R.emitted_on: entry to the right consumption WAIT_EXIT
STOP_FLUID_G_R.rationale: Emitted after the solenoid closes (BehaviorBox.h:1051). Modelling it as the entry strobe of the consumption state colocates the actuator close with its strobe -- semantically tidier than the current bracketing, and free.

STOP_FLUID_G_L.emitted_on: entry to the left consumption WAIT_EXIT

ODOR_1_ON.emitted_on: entry to a sampling HOLD bound to odor line 1
ODOR_1_ON.rationale: Stimulus identity. This is the one state whose entry code identifies WHAT was presented, which is why it is a per-trial @binding rather than a fixed field.

ODOR_2_ON.emitted_on: entry to a sampling HOLD bound to odor line 2

ODOR_3_ON.emitted_on: entry to a sampling HOLD bound to odor line 3

ODOR_4_ON.emitted_on: entry to a sampling HOLD bound to odor line 4

ODOR_5_ON.emitted_on: entry to a sampling HOLD bound to odor line 5

ODOR_6_ON.emitted_on: entry to a sampling HOLD bound to odor line 6

RESP_OMIT.rationale: Firmware used to emit NOTHING when the response window expired, so an omission was only inferable from the absence of a poke before END_INCORRECT_ITI -- and END_INCORRECT_ITI is reached by three different outcomes, so the class was recoverable only from the PRECEDING strobe, which an omission has none of. BehaviorBox.h's checkResponse() emits it now. Sessions recorded before that change still carry the silence.

ODOR_7_ON.emitted_on: entry to a sampling HOLD bound to odor line 7
ODOR_7_ON.rationale: Stimulus identity for odor line 7. Twelve lines have always existed in the pinout but only six could announce an onset, so lines 7-12 were plumbed and unusable as discriminanda. Numbered to continue 101-106 as closely as the reserved block allows -- see ODOR_10_ON for the gap.

ODOR_8_ON.emitted_on: entry to a sampling HOLD bound to odor line 8
ODOR_8_ON.rationale: Stimulus identity for odor line 8. Twelve lines have always existed in the pinout but only six could announce an onset, so lines 7-12 were plumbed and unusable as discriminanda. Numbered to continue 101-106 as closely as the reserved block allows -- see ODOR_10_ON for the gap.

ODOR_9_ON.emitted_on: entry to a sampling HOLD bound to odor line 9
ODOR_9_ON.rationale: Stimulus identity for odor line 9. Twelve lines have always existed in the pinout but only six could announce an onset, so lines 7-12 were plumbed and unusable as discriminanda. Numbered to continue 101-106 as closely as the reserved block allows -- see ODOR_10_ON for the gap.

ODOR_10_ON.emitted_on: entry to a sampling HOLD bound to odor line 10
ODOR_10_ON.rationale: Stimulus identity for odor line 10, and the code that carries the reason for the gap. Lines 7-9 continue the original run at 107-109; 110-113 are RETIRED (the dummy solenoid clicks, present in 29 recorded sessions) and can never be reissued, so the run resumes at 114. This is why nothing may compute an odor's code from its index.

ODOR_11_ON.emitted_on: entry to a sampling HOLD bound to odor line 11
ODOR_11_ON.rationale: Stimulus identity for odor line 11. Twelve lines have always existed in the pinout but only six could announce an onset, so lines 7-12 were plumbed and unusable as discriminanda. Numbered to continue 101-106 as closely as the reserved block allows -- see ODOR_10_ON for the gap.

ODOR_12_ON.emitted_on: entry to a sampling HOLD bound to odor line 12
ODOR_12_ON.rationale: Stimulus identity for odor line 12. Twelve lines have always existed in the pinout but only six could announce an onset, so lines 7-12 were plumbed and unusable as discriminanda. Numbered to continue 101-106 as closely as the reserved block allows -- see ODOR_10_ON for the gap.

_why: Slot -> the six codes a response port on that slot reports with.
TWO SLOTS, BECAUSE THE TRIAL RUNNER HAS TWO PORTS. BehaviorBox.h's
checkResponse() polls rightWell and leftWell; there is no third to poll, so a
third slot would be a promise the firmware cannot keep. Slots 3-7 were declared
here for a task-graph interpreter that was removed, and their thirty codes were
Slots 1 and 2 point at the historical _L and _R names, so a recorded session
decodes exactly as it always did.
This table is why nothing downstream derives a code from a channel called
'left_well'. It used to: a _SIDE map and a matching sideSuffix() in the frontend
meant a box whose wells were named anything else silently got no per-port codes

_readme: Codes that were emitted by firmware this repository no longer contains, and
which MUST NOT be reused. This is the third state: neither declared (nothing
emits them) nor free (`free_ranges` excludes them), and `is_free()` consults
both.
THE ENTRY CONDITION IS THAT A REAL SESSION CONTAINS THEM. That is what
separates this section from deletion -- 24,600 recorded events carry the codes
below, and reissuing one would silently merge two unrelated event types in any
analysis that spans the boundary. A code declared for firmware that never ran
was reclaimed instead; see the note in the file's own readme.
The replay validator recognises them by name so a legacy session reports
'retired code' rather than 'unknown code' -- a distinction that matters,
because one is explained and the other is a question.

DUMMY_SOLENOID_CLICK_1.rationale: Dummy solenoid click. Emitted between a terminal and the next LIGHTS_ON to mask the audible cue of the real odor valve, so a subject could not use valve noise to predict the trial.
